name: The Fallout Belt
roomText: A ruined city block, downwind of the site. The evac routes were never used.
You're in a stripped maintenance shop. A faded government notice is taped to the till.
The street has collapsed into its own rubble. Nothing has been cleared in years.
A flickering streetlamp buzzes over cracked asphalt and long grass.
Broken glass crunches underfoot outside a gutted storefront.
A checkpoint stands abandoned, its barrier arm frozen halfway down.
Chalk arrows on the walls point the way to a relief centre that isn't there.
You come around a corner into a plaza where every window faces the same blast direction.

name: The Rust Quarter
roomText: Everything here has rusted to the same flaking orange.
A collapsed overpass makes a low iron ceiling you have to stoop under.
Stripped vehicle husks are stacked three high along the kerb.
Something drips, steady and metallic, somewhere in the dark.
A row of shipping containers has been welded into a shanty and then abandoned again.
Rebar juts from every broken slab like reeds from a riverbed.
A salvage crew's tally is scratched into a girder, the last mark half-finished.
The wind moves through a hundred empty window frames and makes a low chord.

name: The Neon Undercity
roomText: Flickering signage buzzes over a flooded transit platform.
Rusted turnstiles block a half-collapsed tunnel mouth.
A vending machine hums, still lit, offering nothing anyone recognises.
Graffiti covers every surface of this junction, layer on layer on layer.
Dead screens line the wall, all showing the same frozen frame of a news desk.
An escalator runs backward into standing water, forever.
Riot shielding is stacked against a doorway from the inside.
A departures board cycles through destinations that are all just numbers now.

name: The Drowned Sprawl
roomText: Black water laps at your knees in the gap between two leaning towers.
A rooftop garden has gone under and become a reeking green swamp.
Drowned traffic lights still cycle, red to green, below the surface.
Something large turns over in the water further out, and is gone.
You wade through what was a shopping arcade; the shopfront glass holds.
A ferry lies on its side across the road, hull opened like a tin.
Fishing lines run from a high window down into the murk, taut and old.
The tidemark on the walls is well above your head and still rising.

name: The Ashfall Wastes
roomText: Ash drifts in slow spirals over a dead six-lane highway.
A skeletal billboard frame creaks in a wind that never fully stops.
Grey sand has swallowed half of what was once a civic plaza.
The ground is warm underfoot here, and nothing grows.
Dunes the colour of cigarette ash roll to the horizon in every direction.
A convoy sits nose to tail on the shoulder, tyres gone, doors open.
You pass a relief tent, still pegged out, filled to the roof with drift.
The sun is a pale coin behind the haze and gives almost no heat.

name: The Deep Archive
roomText: The ceiling is lost somewhere far above you in the dark.
Pale roots hang through the cracks in the poured-stone walls.
A vast buried hall, its pillars worn smooth by decades of seeping water.
Your footsteps come back to you a half-second later than they should.
Rows of sealed record vaults recede into black, their labels gone.
A reading room, chairs still pushed in, every book fused into one grey brick.
Somewhere down a side passage, a machine is still filing, patiently.
The air is dead and cool and smells faintly of paper and rust.

name: The Buried Reaches
roomText: Flooded galleries stretch away beneath the weight of the world.
Bioluminescent scum lights the water a faint, sick green.
A drift of ruined books has silted up the mouth of a side chamber.
The pressure in your ears never quite equalises, however you swallow.
Stairs go down into the water and keep going, past where the light gives out.
A drowned checkpoint, its logbook still chained to the desk, pages pulped.
Cave pearls the size of fists line a channel cut by nothing natural.
You hear a bell, very deep, very slow, and then you don't.

name: The Frostbound Vaults
roomText: Frost has grown over every surface in feathered white sheets.
A sealed blast door, rimed shut, stands a hand's width open.
Your breath hangs in front of you and does not disperse.
Ice-locked machinery lines the walls, dials stopped at the same reading.
Something under the clear ice of the floor has the shape of a hand.
Cold-storage racks stretch away, each cradle empty, each tag frosted blank.
A generator hall, the turbines furred with rime, silent.
Icicles have grown up from the floor to meet the ones coming down.

name: The Glacier Deeps
roomText: A blue-black crevasse drops away past the reach of your light.
The walls here are old ice, packed with trapped bubbles like held breath.
A frozen river hangs mid-fall down the throat of the shaft.
It is so cold that the air itself feels solid in your lungs.
A research hut is entombed in the glacier, lamps still burning inside the ice.
You cross a bridge of blue ice over nothing you can see the bottom of.
Meltwater runs somewhere below, the only moving thing for miles.
The ice pops and cracks around you, settling, always settling.

name: The Shattered Orbital
roomText: A ring corridor curves up and away from you in both directions.
Stars wheel slowly past a cracked observation port.
Loose debris drifts through the failed artificial gravity like snow.
Warning placards float unmoored in the dead, still air.
The hull groans, low and long, as the station's spin decays.
An evacuation muster point, harness straps hanging open, pods all gone.
A hydroponics bay, its racks black and dry, a single light still cycling.
Earth is a smudge in the port, or it isn't there at all; hard to say.

name: The Vacuum Reaches
roomText: Torn hull plating opens directly onto absolute black.
Everything not bolted down has long since drifted out and away.
Frozen atmosphere coats the bulkheads in a fur of white crystal.
The sound of your own breathing is the only sound there is.
A blast shutter has half-closed on a body-shaped absence of frost.
Cabling hangs in slow, frozen arcs across the passage.
A hatch stands open on a compartment that is simply gone.
Your suit ticks as it warms the metal you touch, then cools again.

name: The Chronofracture
roomText: Reality stutters here; the same moment happens twice, then a third time.
A corridor folds back into itself, and you walk out of the door you walked in.
Shards of frozen time hang in the air like panes of broken glass.
You see yourself, a room away, not yet arrived.
The light reaches you before whatever cast it does.
A clock on the wall runs backwards, forwards, and stops, in that order.
Your footprints are already ahead of you, leading on.
This is close to the tear the Tunnel opened. The air hums with it.

name: The Long Now
roomText: Every clock in the room reads a different century, and all of them are right.
Dust falls upward, slowly, and settles in a grey coat on the ceiling.
A single instant, stretched thin enough that you can walk around inside it.
Nothing here has moved in ten thousand years. Including, until now, you.
A candle burns with a flame that doesn't flicker and doesn't shorten.
You pour water from a canteen and it hangs, a rope of it, not falling.
The far wall is a century away and you will never reach it walking.
Sound takes so long to arrive that the silence has texture.

name: The Final Instant
roomText: The end of the timeline is a white, soundless room with no far side.
There is no 'next' here. There is only this.
Everything that will ever happen has already finished happening.
The air tastes of the last second before a storm that will not break.
Your shadow has nowhere to fall and so there isn't one.
You can feel the Tunnel from here, upstream, tiny, still open, still pouring.
This is as far downstream as the fray goes. After this it just stops.
Something is standing very still in the white, and has been, forever.
